title: Weight-Space Programming on Qwen3-ASR-0.6B: Nine Independent Agent Edits, Random-Direction Controls, and a Missing Attention Mask
read_level: full (Zenodo record API + PDF Aslanturk2026_WSP_Qwen3-ASR.pdf via pdftotext; appendix edit table skimmed)
metadata_mismatch: Corpus abstract empty; filled from paper. Record version DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.23976685 (concept DOI 23976684). Title/author match.
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5 agent arms read Qwen3-ASR-0.6B weights and derive analytic edits (head gains, rank-1 removals, k_proj terms) with no gradients, under 10/25/50 forward-pass budgets, to fix a language-ID failure on speech surrounded by silence.
domain: automatic speech recognition (multilingual FLEURS; language tagging under long silence)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) agent instances; Claude Sonnet 5.5 for harness/evaluation; Opus 5.5 orchestrator
interface: code/tensor tools (agent computes analytic edits from weight analysis and difference-of-means activation stats)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (budget of 10, 25 or 50 forward passes of up to 64 practice clips)
self_editing: no; Claude agents edit a separate ASR model
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "The edit sizes range from 2,048 weights (b25, 0.0003%) to 7,225,343 (b50, 0.92%)" (Sec 5.1)

headline_results.claim: All nine edits reduce target failure without breaking clips
headline_results.quote: All nine edits reduce it, with 0 newly broken clips and McNemar p < 0.01 on the combined 70 target clips for every arm
The real edit fixes strictly more clips than every control in 26 of 27 comparisons
Six of nine arms independently localized the same two decoder attention heads (L20H13 and L21H2)
Four arms show a clean macro WER regression whose paired-bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0: b10r3 (+0.32 pp), b25r3 (+0.31), b50 (+0.40) and b50r2 (+0.24)

headline_results.claim: Backend artifact: mask restoration matches best edit
headline_results.quote: Restoring the mask alone fixes 31 of 40 stress and 5 of 30 hard-TS target clips, equal to the best arm (b25r3: 31 and 5) and above the other eight arms on stress-40 (6–28)
Target B (bilingual code-switching) was not fixed
30 of 40 stress target clips are tagged language None

cost.quote: Total passes used per run: b10 10, b10r2 10, b10r3 10, b25 23, b25r2 21, b25r3 15, b50 32, b50r2 27, b50r3 33

cost.claim: Hardware; no token or $ cost reported
cost.quote: All runs on one Apple M3 Max in fp32 with a per-process MPS cap, so a full test evaluation takes hours

baselines_and_controls: Unedited baseline; five random-direction controls per arm matched in tensors, edit form, changed-weight count and Frobenius norm; guard set (40 silence/noise clips); separate windowed-encoder (mask restored, no weight change) analysis.
runs_and_variance: 9 arms (3 replicates x 3 budgets); 5 controls per arm; exact McNemar per arm; paired bootstrap (1000 resamples) for clean WER; mean ± sd per budget (Table 4). Single-use test set.
robustness_of_edits: Edits tested on top of the windowed encoder for 3 original arms: "add at most one more clip"; not tested on FlashAttention-2 path, quantization or fine-tuning.
verification: none formal; single-use test harness refusing re-evaluation; McNemar and bootstrap statistics
memorization_vs_reasoning: Author cautions convergence is not independent evidence: arms "share a model family, a brief that names mechanism families, and the same practice data"; independence for b25 and b50 assumed, not enforced. Only one arm (b50) intervened at the encoder, closest to the true cause.
limitations_stated: Single 0.6B model and one successfully targeted pathology; small synthetic target sets; pathology largely a backend artifact (missing encoder window mask on sdpa/MPS); FA2 untested; agents from one LLM family; five controls per arm; clean WER regressions; in-sample selection on practice data.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, Nov 2026), Experiment 8 protocol
notes_for_survey: Independent replication of the WSP loop-repair protocol on an ASR model with matched random-direction controls; edits beat controls but the failure was mostly caused by a missing attention mask in the inference backend, which restoring without weight changes fixes about as well as the best edit. Distributed failure (code-switching) was not fixable, consistent with the original blog's Gemma result.
